findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated — it subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing any abstract methods
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now declared as `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since none of these are implemented, the class remains abstract, and `Detector.detector_handler` (which calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any Detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty list, so any existing code or test that resolves the handler for a MetricAlertFire detector now crashes instead of no-oping. Either implement stub versions of the abstract methods or keep it on DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation is ready.

findings.title: test_dedupe in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue builds the expected occurrence with group key "val1" but evaluates "group_key", so the fingerprints never match
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, which sets `fingerprint=handler.build_fingerprint("val1")` (i.e. `["<detector_id>:val1"]`). However `evaluate_group_key_value` is then called with group_key `"group_key"`, so the actual result contains an occurrence whose fingerprint is `["<detector_id>:group_key"]`. IssueOccurrence equality compares the fingerprint, so `expected_result == actual` fails. The first argument to build_mock_occurrence_and_event should be `"group_key"` (matching the key passed to evaluate_group_key_value), otherwise this test fails once it runs.

findings.title: test_state_results_multi_group builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with value 6 while the packet gives group_2 a value of 10
findings.body: In test_state_results_multi_group the data packet is `{"dedupe": 2, "group_vals": {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}}`, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` — value 6 instead of 10. The test passes only because the mock occurrence builder currently ignores the `value` argument; if build_occurrence_and_event_data (or the mock) ever incorporates the value into the occurrence/event data, this test would silently assert the wrong expectation. Pass 10 to match the packet.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring on `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but this PR changed the signature to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. The stale docstring contradicts the new contract and will mislead anyone implementing a subclass.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment claims the handler will be a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'
findings.body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` sits directly above MetricAlertDetectorHandler, but this PR just made it subclass StatefulDetectorHandler — so it already is a stateful detector (an unimplemented, abstract one). The comment now describes the opposite of the code and should be updated or removed.
